messages:
maya_infra: Heads up — seeing a sharp p95 jump between GPU nodes in us-west during the noon batching window. 6ms -> ~120ms, packet loss visible, RDMA retransmit counters climbing. Started ~11:58, peaked ~12:05, affecting several TF jobs. Anyone on this? :thinking:

sam_ops: Which racks/ToRs and is this inter-AZ or same AZ? Any config changes rolled recently?

maya_infra: rack-r32 -> rack-r33, same AZ. No infra deploys at that time in staging but k8s node kubelet updates went out last night. No config change I know of to NICs.

joel_sre: Can you paste the RDMA/IB counters and a quick ethtool snapshot? Also check for kernel log messages around link resets.

maya_infra: Paste from the affected host (sanitized):
```
# ibv_query_port mlx5_0 1
link_layer: IB
port_state: PORT_ACTIVE
rx_pkts: 12456789
tx_pkts: 12456000
rx_discards: 3
recv_errors: 12
retransmits: 842
# ethtool -S eth0 | egrep -i "tx_|rx_|retry"
tx_errors: 0
tx_retries: 410
rx_missed: 7
```
Also saw repeat of this in dmesg around 11:59: `mlx5_core: port 1 reset (link down/up)` x3.

katie_platform: We rolled kernel 6.1.0-9 to rack-r33 nodes at 02:00am last night. rack-r32 stayed on previous kernel. Could be an MTU/driver mismatch surfaced by sustained batching load.

sam_ops: That fits — mixing kernel/driver versions can change default offloads or MTU handling. Have you confirmed MTU on both ToRs?

maya_infra: Checked quickly: rack-r32 ToR eth0 shows mtu 9000, rack-r33 ToR eth0 shows mtu 1500. Oof.

joel_sre: There you go — jumbo mismatch across the east-west path will cause fragmentation or fallback and push RDMA into retransmits under high throughput. For now, either set rack-r33 ToR to 9000 or temporarily lower the compute NIC MTU to 1500 until we schedule a proper change.

sam_ops: Agree. Quick mitigation: set ToR on rack-r33 to 9000 (if switch supports it) and bump NIC MTU. Also check for any middleboxes doing MSS clamping.

maya_infra: Applying temp fix: running `sudo ip link set dev eth0 mtu 9000` on the k8s nodes in rack-r33 and asked neteng to flip ToR MTU. Will report back.

(1 minute later) maya_infra: quick grab after change: p95 back down to ~8ms, retransmits dropped to single digits. Looks like the MTU change helped. :thumbsup:

katie_platform: We need a rollout plan to align kernel/driver + switch MTU across racks so this doesn't happen again. I'll file a runbook and a postmortem.

joel_sre: Also add an automated alert for sudden inter-node retransmit rate > X and an MTU drift checker in the infra health job. Could prevent recurrence.

rdma_bot: Alert cleared at 12:14 UTC — inter-node RDMA retransmit spike resolved.

maya_infra: Thanks everyone. I'll coordinate with neteng for scheduled ToR change and add a node-level MTU check to the preflight for kernel rollouts.

sam_ops: Nice catch. Marking as resolved for now, but keep an eye during tomorrow's peak window.

katie_platform: Will add to platform changelog and sync with SRE on mitigation steps.

joel_sre: If we see similar patterns in other racks, consider adding an MTU policy check into the autoscaler so nodes with mismatched MTU don't get scheduled for latency-sensitive GPU batches.

maya_infra: adding notes to the incident ticket. Ending thread. :white_check_mark:
